d: The extended range is enabled only on newer Cisco devices.

e: shutdown under (config-vlan), or (config)# shutdown vlan n
d: A common cause of "VLAN not working" faults — check the VLAN hasn't been shut down, and neither has its SVI.

e: 802.1Q is the IEEE standard; ISL (Inter-Switch Link) is Cisco-proprietary and deprecated
d: Dot1q is the only supported option on newer switch models — entering the encapsulation command gives an error because it's non-configurable there.

e: Forces a port to never trunk
d: Disables DTP negotiation on that port.

e: Forces a port to always trunk

d: Trunks if the other side is set to trunk or dynamic desirable; access otherwise. Two dynamic-auto ports facing each other result in access mode.

e: Default mode on older switches; actively initiates trunking negotiation
d: Trunks if the other side is dynamic auto, dynamic desirable, or trunk. Two dynamic-desirable ports facing each other result in a trunk.
Negotiates trunking dynamically. DTP frames travel over the native VLAN, so native VLAN settings must match on both switches. A link fails if one side is set to trunk and the other to access.

e: If VTP is enabled (even in transparent mode), the VTP domain name must match on both switches for DTP to succeed
d: A subtle gotcha: two switches can otherwise be correctly configured for trunking and still fail to form one because of a VTP domain mismatch.

e: Restricts which VLANs are allowed to pass over a trunk
d: Can be specified multiple times to build up the allowed list.

e: Shows all trunking ports, including VLANs allowed on each port and VLANs pruned by Spanning Tree
d: show interfaces ifname switchport shows the settings (access/trunk/voice VLAN etc.) of one given port.

e: Lets a single switch port carry both an IP phone's voice traffic and an attached PC's data traffic
d: The phone has a built-in internal switch that trunks the voice VLAN and access VLAN traffic upstream, even though the switch port itself is configured as an access port.

e: switchport mode access + switchport access vlan x + switchport voice vlan y
d: x is the data/access VLAN for the attached PC; y is the dedicated voice VLAN for the phone itself.

Synchronises VLAN information (IDs and names) between switches on a trunk. It's recommended to disable it (vtp mode transparent or off), since a single misconfiguration can add, change or remove VLANs across the whole campus.

e: Default mode; creates/modifies/deletes VLANs, stores them in NVRAM, and originates and forwards VTP advertisements
Listens for and forwards VTP advertisements; cannot add, modify or delete VLANs locally, and its VLAN database is not stored in NVRAM
Does not originate advertisements or use them to populate its own VLAN database, but does forward them between other switches
d: Maintains its own VLAN database in NVRAM. This is the recommended mode — manually configure identical VLANs on every switch instead.

e: If an external switch with a higher configuration revision number joins the network, it overwrites VLAN configuration on all switches and can destroy campus-wide connectivity
d: Whichever VTP server has the highest configuration revision number becomes the one whose advertisements are used by everyone else.

e: VTPv3 designates one VTP server as primary; other servers act as clients in all but name and can't originate config changes
d: Solves the VTP bomb problem. Primary status can be password protected. VTPv3 also supports extended VLANs (1006-4094) and propagates MST instance information, unlike VTPv1/v2.
